about: Pre-registered story-pocket targets per locality scenario: roles, occurrence bands, size targets and story frequencies. Read by tools/showcase-scoreboard.mjs. Generated, not hand-typed: change a rule or an override in tools/story-pocket-targets.mjs and rewrite.

rules.status: PROPOSED by Claude 2026-10-22; awaiting the boss. The rules are design choices; the evidence each target rests on is cited per entry.
rules.wanted_share_basis: A species is wanted from a locality when it holds at least 5 % of the locality's record (Mineralienatlas photographs and eBay listings, compare.json "real"), as the scoreboard has used since 2026-10-21. Where the record is too thin to vote, the collectibles the sources name (named_signatures).
rules.occurrence: A run in which at least one crystal of the species survives (census n_surv > 0), at any size.
rules.occurrence_bands_basis: The literature's abundance class for the deposit (proposals/DATA-LOCALITY-ABUNDANCE-2026-10-21.json, literature), read as the share of story pockets the species occurs in: abundant 50–95 %, common 30–90 %, uncommon 10–60 %, rare 2–30 %, very rare at most 15 %. No class reaches 100 %: signature minerals should be "common, not guaranteed" (the boss, 2026-10-22), and the supporting cast "usually present". The numbers are a design choice, not measured. With 21 seeds one species in every seed is within noise of a 90–95 % ceiling, so the scoreboard also tests the fleet: how many species occur in every seed, against the chance of that if each occurred at its ceiling. A form suffix (-crust, -coating, -oxidized) keeps the class. doc (documented without an abundance word), ND, ND?, Q and no class leave the band unresolved. Photograph and listing shares are never used: they measure collector salience, not geological frequency.
rules.visible_basis: The locality review's "visible" (a crystal of at least 1 mm not flagged as enclosed), kept as a reporting convention: the dust and hidden flags use it, and the clutter share reads the census's count of such crystals (n_1_exp), which the census takes at exactly 1 mm — so this value cannot change and the scoreboard refuses any other. It decides no verdict and is not a size target.
rules.specimen_min_basis: A specimen length below this is set aside: micromount captions give the crystal or the field of view as "Größe" ("Malachit ; Größe: 4,2 mm"), and a misread crystal would pull a specimen proxy below the crystals it is meant to bound. A cabinet or thumbnail specimen is longer.
rules.specimen_joins: Two photographs of one species are one specimen when uploaded together (ids within uploaded_together_s) with the same caption stretches (identical once a word cut at the stretch's start, punctuation and the words "mit", "und", "auf" are dropped) or the same multi-dimension length of a crystal, an aggregate or the specimen (a picture's size joins nothing); or, uploaded apart, when they state the same length in three dimensions, one written with a decimal ("5x5x4,8mm", "15,9 x 10 x 4,7 cm"); never when their captions name different finds, or when each names a mineral the other does not ("mit etwas Limonit" against "mit etwas Hämatit"). A generic caption ("BB 4,5 mm") or a round size repeated years apart counts as two specimens. Every join is listed in proposals/DATA-STORY-POCKET-SIZES-2026-10-22.md.
rules.series: Lengths of one kind (crystal or specimen) in one wording once the numbers are taken out (seriesKey, tools/story-pocket-lib.mjs) whose specimens were uploaded in one stretch — each less than series_gap_s after the one before (largestSeries) — are one series: likely one contributor's lot or find, not independent samples. The capture has no uploader names, so the stretch stands in for the contributor. A standard caption field ("Größe: #", "Kristallgröße: #", "Size #": isFieldLabel) is everyone's wording, so only photographs uploaded together (within uploaded_together_s) make a series of it. When the largest series holds more than half of a crystal target's lengths, its confidence drops one step; every target records its quantiles without its largest series, so the scoreboard can say whether a verdict rests on it.
rules.series_gap_basis: A year: longer than the gaps inside the runs of one unusual wording that are plainly one contributor's (a lot photographed over months), shorter than the gaps at which standard wordings recur (years). The appendix gives each largest series' span in days.
rules.size_basis: Photographed lengths (proposals/DATA-STORY-POCKET-SIZES-CAPTURE-2026-10-22.json, classed by tools/story-pocket-size-evidence.mjs). Photographs of one specimen count once (specimen_joins). Each specimen gives one value per kind: its largest stated crystal of the species. With at least size_min_samples specimens, a crystal target: confidence low below size_medium_confidence, medium below size_high_confidence, high from it, one step lower when one series dominates (series). Otherwise the specimens' dimensions (none below specimen_min_mm), if at least size_min_samples, as a proxy, confidence low: a specimen is at least as long as its own crystals, so the proxy overstates the crystal — reaching it is strong evidence (not proof: the photographs that state crystal lengths and those that state specimen sizes are different subsets), falling short of it is none. Otherwise unknown. There is no default size. Materials collected as pieces (tiger's eye, chrysoprase, chalcedony, jasper) have piece sizes only, so at best a proxy.
rules.display_range_basis: The record's quantiles that bound its display scale: a crystal from the record's lower quartile to its 90th percentile is at the scale the record shows; past the 90th it is oversize. A fresh crystal from the record's population lands inside the range of a record of n crystals with probability 0.65 × (n − 1) / (n + 1) (displayCoverage: exact for a uniform population, within about 0.03 and on the low side for lognormal ones): 0.43 at n = 5, 0.58 at n = 17. That coverage enters the story frequency (story_frequency_rule). The scoreboard reads the targets' q25 and q90 and refuses another range.
rules.size_check: Per run, the species' largest crystal not flagged as enclosed (census max_exp_mm). The record's median is the characteristic crystal, its quartiles the range: a crystal in the display range (q25–q90) is at the record's display scale; past q90 it is oversize. Over the runs where the species occurs in a cavity that holds its median, the median of those crystals against the record: BELOW (< q25), MEETS (q25–q75, around the record's median), LARGE (q75–q90), OVERSIZE (> q90). Against a proxy: BELOW PROXY (< q25, not a verdict), REACHES PROXY (q25–q90; oversize cannot be tested against a proxy), OVERSIZE (> q90). A crystal longer than the cavity's span is left out and flagged: the starting cavity cannot hold it.
rules.eligibility: A cavity can hold a species' characteristic crystal when its span — the longest distance between two wall vertices (tools/story-pocket-cavities.mjs) — is at least the target's median. The span is an upper bound on the longest crystal the cavity holds (in a cavity that is not convex the chord can cross the wall), so SMALL is conclusive and STORY-SCALE is generous. A pocket is SMALL when it cannot hold the primary protagonist's characteristic crystal: it may lack a showcase and is left out of the story frequency (its stories are reported apart). The locality's target is never shrunk to fit the cavity. A pocket is UNCLASSED when this cannot be told (the primary's size is unknown, or a proxy longer than the cavity): a run without a story there may be a small pocket, so it stays open rather than counting against the story.
rules.story_frequency_rule: A run carries the story when an intended protagonist (the primary or an alternate) occurs with its largest unflagged crystal in its record's display range and no longer than the cavity. The scenario should carry it in at least floor × coverage of its scored runs, for the protagonist that can carry a story run with the largest such product: floor = its band's lower bound; coverage = the chance that a crystal drawn from its record's population lands in the display range of a record of its size (display_range_basis). A protagonist can carry a story run when it has an engine, a band and a size target whose display range starts within the scenario's cavity span (q25 ≤ cavity_span_mm: the same test a run's YES needs; the size verdict's eligibility uses the median instead, and the scoreboard shows the verdicts under that test too). One with no size target, or a range that starts beyond the span, does not set the frequency. Crystal targets come first: a proxy sets the frequency only where no crystal target can carry a story run, as a size target prefers crystal lengths. For a crystal target the frequency is the expected story rate of a fleet whose protagonist occurs at its band's floor with crystals drawn from the record: an expectation, not a guarantee — with 21 seeds such a fleet falls short about half the time, and the verdict marks a shortfall its interval cannot tell from the frequency "noise" (noise_z). For a specimen proxy it is a bar for STORY (PROXY), the rate at which crystals as large as the photographed specimens would reach the proxy's range — not an expected rate, since the proxy overstates the crystal. The coverage is never cut to the cavity: runs whose crystal is longer than it stay open, so a cavity shorter than the range's top leaves the verdict open rather than failing it. But the cavity does decide which protagonists can carry a story run, so dropping one whose range starts beyond the span can lower the frequency (Elmwood) or remove it; each basis names the protagonists dropped, and the scoreboard lists them. It asks for no protagonist in every seed or size spread narrower than the record's. Unresolved when no protagonist can carry a story run, or when runs whose protagonist has no known crystal target, or whose pocket is unclassed, could still carry it. The story verdict checks this alone; WP1's whole target also needs every protagonist within its band, the protagonist that carries the story at the record's size (its typical crystal within the record's middle half) and none oversize (the scoreboard reports both).
rules.noise_basis: The Wilson score interval at z 1.96 (95 %). An occurrence rate outside its band is "noise" when its interval still reaches the band. A story shortfall is noise when the interval of the runs that carry or could carry the story (yes + open: an open run might have carried it) still reaches the frequency — except where no protagonist with an engine occurs in any seed: then chance in which runs carry the story explains nothing, and there is no noise mark. 21 runs cannot tell a noise shortfall from the target. Noise marks a verdict; it does not change it, except that WP1's target counts a band miss within noise as within.
rules.clutter_basis: WP3's target: visible clutter (crystals of species with no photograph, no listing and no literature at the locality) under 10 % of a scenario's visible crystals. The scoreboard flags a scenario at or above it and lists it in the clutter table.
rules.star_basis: WP2's target: the star (the species of a run's largest unflagged crystal) is a wanted species, any role but companion, in at least half the runs; a companion as the star in half the runs or more is the supporting cast in the star's place. The scoreboard flags a scenario below it and counts the scenarios on either side.
rules.variety: A scenario should give a distribution of pockets, not one assemblage every run (the boss, 2026-10-22). The scoreboard reports, per scenario, the distinct assemblages (sets of surviving species) across its seeds, the protagonists present in every seed, and how much each protagonist's largest crystal varies (interquartile range over median, beside the record's); and, for the fleet, the chance that every species seen in all its seeds would be if each occurred at its band's ceiling.
rules.roles: From the record, gated by the literature (deriveRoles, tools/story-pocket-lib.mjs): primary = the most-wanted species the literature does not contradict (ND, ND?, Q) or call rare (RA, VR); alternate = every other such wanted species; showpiece = a wanted species the literature calls rare; unsupported = a wanted species the literature contradicts (listed, not targeted); companion = a species the literature calls abundant or common that the record does not want (the supporting cast: it should occur, not be the star). Species the comparison sets aside as outside the scenario's scope have no role.
rules.companions_and_showpieces: Companions are scored on occurrence against their band and on not being the star; showpieces on occurrence against their band and, where a size target exists, on how often they reach it. Neither carries the story.
rules.uploaded_together_basis: Mineralienatlas image ids read as upload times in seconds since 1970: the 2217 captured ids run from 1094647902 (2004-09-08) to 1792434360 (2026-10-19), 2 days before the capture (2026-10-22). 1,000,000 s is about 11.6 days. The site does not document the ids; this is an inference.
